en.name: Bottled marinade
en.summary: Bottled marinade is a commercial mix of oil, acid, salt and seasoning sold to be poured over raw meat. Unopened it keeps about 1 year from purchase in the cupboard; after opening, refrigerate it and use it within about 6 months. The real safety question is not the bottle but what happens after it touches raw meat.
en.pantry: An unopened bottle keeps about 1 year from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard, away from the hob and out of the sun. The acid and salt keep it stable while the seal holds. Once it is open, it belongs in the fridge. Never marinate food on the counter — marinating happens in the refrigerator, in a covered dish or a sealed bag, not at room temperature, however short the recipe says.
en.fridge: Once opened, keep the bottle at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use within about 6 months. The habit that matters most is to pour out what you need into a bowl rather than dipping or brushing from the bottle: once the marinade has touched raw meat, poultry or fish, it is raw-meat liquid and must never go back into the bottle. If you want to use some as a sauce, set aside a clean portion before the meat goes anywhere near it, or boil the used marinade thoroughly before serving it.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for bottled marinade and there is little reason to freeze something that keeps for months. It will also separate — oil-and-acid mixtures split on thawing and need shaking hard to come back. A more useful trick is to freeze meat in its marinade: the meat marinates as it thaws in the fridge, and the marinade goes into the bin with the bag rather than into a sauce.
en.thawing: Thaw meat that was frozen in marinade in the fridge, never on the counter, and discard the used marinade unless you boil it first.
spoilage: Mould around the neck, the cap or on the surface
A fermented, yeasty or alcoholic smell
Separation that will not shake back together, with a rancid smell from the oil
A bottle that fizzes or spurts when opened
tips: Pour what you need into a bowl; never brush straight from the bottle.
Set aside a clean portion for serving before the meat touches any of it.
Marinate in the fridge in a covered dish or sealed bag, never on the counter.
Freeze meat and marinade together in a flat bag for an easy weeknight meal.

faq.q: How long does bottled marinade last once opened?
faq.a: About 6 months refrigerated at 4 °C or below. Unopened, about 1 year from purchase in the cupboard.

faq.q: Can you reuse marinade that has touched raw meat?
faq.a: Not as it is. It is raw-meat liquid. Boil it thoroughly before using it as a sauce, or better, set aside a clean portion beforehand.

faq.q: Can you marinate food on the counter?
faq.a: No. Marinate in the fridge in a covered dish or sealed bag; the counter puts the meat in the danger zone.
No timeline is given and it separates on thawing. Freezing meat in its marinade is the more useful version of the idea.

zh.name: 瓶裝醃醬
zh.summary: 瓶裝醃醬是市售的油、酸、鹽和調味料混合物，設計用來淋在生肉上。未開封放櫥櫃，從購買日起算大約 1 年；開封後請冷藏，並在大約 6 個月內用完。真正的安全問題不在瓶子，而在它碰到生肉之後。
zh.pantry: 未開封的瓶子放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃、遠離爐火與日曬，從購買日起算大約 1 年。只要封口完好，酸和鹽就能維持它的穩定。一旦開封，它就屬於冰箱。絕對不要在檯面上醃肉——醃漬要在冰箱裡、用有蓋容器或密封袋進行，不管食譜寫的時間多短都一樣。
zh.fridge: 開封後請放 4 °C 以下，並在大約 6 個月內用完。最重要的習慣是：把需要的量先倒到碗裡，不要直接從瓶口沾或刷。醃醬一旦碰過生肉、家禽或魚，它就是生肉汁，絕對不能倒回瓶子。想拿一部分當淋醬的話，請在肉還沒靠近之前先分出乾淨的一份；否則用過的醃醬一定要徹底煮沸才能上桌。
zh.freezer: 瓶裝醃醬沒有提供冷凍期限，而且一個能放好幾個月的東西也沒什麼冷凍的理由。它還會分離——油和酸的混合物解凍後會分層，要用力搖才回得來。更實用的做法是把肉和醃醬一起冷凍：肉在冷藏解凍的過程中就醃好了，而醃醬連同袋子一起丟掉，不會變成醬汁。
zh.thawing: 和醃醬一起冷凍的肉請放冷藏解凍，絕對不要放室溫；用過的醃醬除非徹底煮沸，否則一律丟棄。
spoilage: 聞起來有發酵味、酵母味或酒味
分層搖不回去，油還帶油耗味
tips: 把要用的量倒到碗裡；絕對不要直接從瓶子刷。
肉碰到之前，先分出乾淨的一份留著當淋醬。
醃漬要在冰箱、用有蓋容器或密封袋，不要在檯面上。
把肉和醃醬一起平放冷凍，平日晚餐會輕鬆很多。

faq.q: 瓶裝醃醬開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 放 4 °C 以下冷藏大約 6 個月。未開封在櫥櫃從購買日起算大約 1 年。

faq.q: 碰過生肉的醃醬還能用嗎？
faq.a: 原樣不行，它就是生肉汁。要當醬汁一定要徹底煮沸，更好的做法是事先分出乾淨的一份。
不行。請在冰箱裡用有蓋容器或密封袋醃；檯面會讓肉落入危險溫度帶。
沒有提供期限，而且解凍後會分離。把肉和醃醬一起冷凍才是比較實用的做法。
